extracted.subtask_description: Practical, prescriptive guidance for a teacher's first days in a primary/district school: how to prepare beforehand, open the school, begin exercises, organize pupils, and observe and manage early discipline. Emphasizes rapport-building, restoring routine, and careful observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induce pupils to seek general information
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of certain exercises is to induce pupils to seek general information in an easy and pleasant manner, as by the perusal of books, newspapers, periodicals, and conversation with friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exercises that encourage care and attention in reading and discrimination in selecting useful facts; call individuals to express ideas verbally so they acquire power of clear and confident expression. (From: 'The object of this exercise is to induce pupils to seek for general information... As individuals are called upon, also, to express their ideas verbally...')

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop oral expression through class exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Give pupils repeated practice in expressing ideas verbally to build clearness, force, ease, and confidence in communicating knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include activities where individuals must speak in front of the class; provide frequent, low-stakes oral opportunities so pupils gain facility (text emphasizes practice by being called on to express ideas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce organized singing with appointed leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is sufficient voice and willing singers, introduce singing as a regular part of devotional exercises by obtaining singing books, appointing a chorister, and forming a Singing Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chorister should decide what tune to sing each day, inform the teacher of metre, and lead the exercise; appoint one or two assistants to relieve embarrassment in starting; allow scholars to bring hymn books; the Committee should manage the singing themselves. (Example: initial hesitation replaced by committee-managed daily singing.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'Tabu' labels to protect delicate or valuable objects
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent damage from handling, place a conspicuous label (Tabu) on rare or delicate specimens/ apparatus to indicate they must not be touched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain to pupils why the label is used (e.g., many hands would injure a rare flower) so the rule is scrupulously regarded; subtle management like this often works better than scolding or watchful precautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze pupils' mental methods (mental analysis of arithmetic work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe and classify the differing methods pupils use to perform tasks (e.g., addition) to understand differences in speed and to instruct more effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run timed experiments, ask pupils to describe or demonstrate their methods, and use the observations to determine whether slowness is due to method rather than lack of skill. (Example: timing different pupils doing an addition problem to reveal method-based speed differences.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach and prefer memory-based mastery (commitment of basic tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage committing basic arithmetic facts (e.g., the addition table) to memory because memory-based recall yields vastly greater speed and efficiency than repeated counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare methods: counting (finger/mental), calculating (doubling, regrouping, adding ten then subtracting one, making ten), and memory; recommend spending time now to fix facts 'once for all' so results come to mind instantly rather than repeatedly counting up hundreds of times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnose and teach multiple calculation strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Be familiar with and teach several calculation strategies (doubling, skip-adding, adding ten minus one, making tens) and help pupils adopt the most efficient methods appropriate to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain and demonstrate the varieties (doubling and adjusting, grouping easily-added numbers, adding ten then subtracting one, transferring to make tens) and note pitfalls (e.g., skip-adding can cause confusion or omission). Use classroom questioning to discover which pupils use which strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep journals of observations and experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers should record experiments, incidents, and observations illustrating educational principles or pupils' tendencies to make study of mind a daily duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping a record facilitates careful practice based on observation, improves interest and efficiency in teaching, and transforms teaching into the study of human nature. (Encouraged: 'The foregoing narratives...may induce some of the readers...to keep journals of their own experiments...')

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather local intelligence about the district before starting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before commencing, obtain as much information as possible about the district: principal families, characters, expectations for school government, previous teachers' methods, complaints, and families likely to cause difficulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain this information privately and discreetly; use it to avoid hostile attitudes and to 'accommodate himself to the character and expectations of his employers' rather than to confront them. This preparation is likened to a navigator learning the sea before sailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converse with older or intelligent scholars/families to learn internal routines
rubrics_metrics.description: Visit or speak with older scholars and families the day/evening before school to learn internal arrangements: textbooks used, principal classes, system of discipline, rewards, and punishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, make a catalogue of principal classes with names and usual order of recitation; these interviews also build rapport and may soften captious families. Use the information to orient early course planning (not necessarily to adopt former methods wholesale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet scholars informally and early to build rapport
rubrics_metrics.description: On the first morning, arrive early and meet pupils in an unofficial, affable manner—converse freely, ask names, enlist help with small tasks—rather than entering with assumed stern dignity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect should be based on real traits of character shown in natural action, not on feigned airs; engaging personally (helping with fire, fixing desks, asking for aid) disarms mischief-makers and creates a 'strong party' in the teacher's favor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open with a sincere devotional exercise unless employers object
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the first day's regular duties with a short religious service (scripture reading, brief explanation, and simple prayer) unless such practice is known to be objectionable to the employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest, heartfelt, simple; avoid feigned solemnity or hackneyed phrases. If unsure about decorum, read a prepared prayer or allow older scholars to read in rotation while ensuring it remains a solemn act, not a mere reading exercise. Respect employers' wishes if they oppose it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore predecessor's routine first, then gradually implement changes
rubrics_metrics.description: For the first few days, ordinarily revive the general routine and order of classes as conducted by the preceding teacher to provide immediate employment and time to observe pupils, then gradually introduce improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a sudden and complete revolution of the school's arrangements; use the predecessor's routine to set pupils at work and then, after observing classes and characters, combine or regroup classes and alter recitation times as needed. In special cases (e.g., private school with prepared plan), a prompt change may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct usual order of exercises by questioning pupils
rubrics_metrics.description: Use directed questioning (e.g., ask what lesson came first, who recited when) to learn the school's usual order and class structure and then set pupils at the customary work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example dialogue: ask if a recitation occurred immediately after school began, how long before recitations, what lessons followed; have pupils identify their classes by standing/sitting and record lists for future use. This provides immediate employment and a memorandum of the ordinary order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the opening period to observe and identify idle/mischievous pupils
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it a special object during the first day or two to discover who the idle and mischievous individuals are, as they tend to seat themselves together and will show themselves early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for small knots of pupils who have seated themselves together; early identification allows the teacher to bring proper authority to bear in due time. Some teachers briefly allow freedom to identify troublemakers, but exercise caution (do not go so far as to abandon control).
